summary: This week's regional landscape was dominated by landmark technological deployments and major financial liquidity developments across the GCC. In Saudi Arabia, the LEAP 2026 conference served as a critical nexus for large-scale enterprise announcements, with tech deals approaching $15 billion—highlighting significant infrastructure commitments from global providers alongside national digital transformation showcases by SDAIA. In banking and payments, Saudi commercial loans expanded by 7% year-to-date to reach $944 billion by July, while the Qatar Central Bank modernized market infrastructure by enabling direct QA-RTGS access for payment service providers. Cross-border regulatory coordination also advanced, with GCC central banks stepping up cybersecurity and fintech cooperation via virtual preparatory committee engagements. Meanwhile, institutional restructuring continued across regional financial sectors, illustrated by shareholders approving the transformation of UGB into Burgan Bank Bahrain, and Kuwait International Bank raising $500 million through a 5-year sukuk issuance. For executives, these developments underscore an accelerating convergence between aggressive capital deployment in enterprise AI infrastructure and tightened cross-border regulatory harmonization.

stories.t: Saudi Arabia tech deals near $15bn as AWS, Microsoft and major AI investments revealed
stories.b: Technology agreements in Saudi Arabia approached $15 billion during LEAP 2026, featuring substantial infrastructure investments from major cloud hyperscalers like AWS and Microsoft, alongside localized artificial intelligence initiatives.
stories.w: Provides massive computational capacity and enterprise software capabilities that will serve as the underlying backbone for regional digital transformation and AI deployment.

stories.t: Saudi banking loans to public and private sectors surge 7% to $944bln by end of July 2026
stories.b: Total banking loans extended to both public and private sectors in Saudi Arabia recorded a 7% increase, reaching $944 billion by the conclusion of July 2026.
stories.w: Reflects robust domestic credit demand and economic liquidity supporting large-scale national infrastructure and corporate expansion projects.

stories.t: Qatar Central Bank Enables Direct QA-RTGS Access for Payment Service Providers
stories.b: The Qatar Central Bank has formally enabled direct access to the Qatar Real Time Gross Settlement system (QA-RTGS) for licensed payment service providers.
stories.w: Dramatically streamlines settlement finality, reduces counterparty risk, and fosters a more competitive and agile fintech ecosystem for payment innovators.

stories.t: GCC central banks step up cybersecurity, fintech co-operation
stories.b: Central banks across the Gulf Cooperation Council have intensified cooperative measures aimed at strengthening regional cybersecurity standards and aligning fintech regulatory frameworks.
stories.w: Essential for maintaining systemic stability, ensuring secure cross-border digital transactions, and protecting critical financial infrastructure from sophisticated threats.

stories.t: Kuwait International Bank raises $500mln with 5-year benchmark sukuk
stories.b: Kuwait International Bank successfully raised $500 million through the issuance of a 5-year benchmark sukuk.
stories.w: Demonstrates healthy international and regional investor appetite for high-grade Islamic fixed-income instruments originating from Kuwaiti financial institutions.

stories.t: UGB shareholders approve proposed transformation into Burgan Bank Bahrain
stories.b: Shareholders of United Gulf Bank (UGB) have voted to approve the company's proposed corporate transformation into Burgan Bank Bahrain.
stories.w: Signals ongoing balance sheet consolidation and structural optimization among regional banking groups seeking operational clarity.

stories.t: Aldar and ADCB complete Abu Dhabi's first off-plan mortgage under new ADREC framework
stories.b: Aldar Properties and Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank finalized Abu Dhabi's inaugural off-plan mortgage transaction operating under the newly implemented ADREC regulatory framework.
stories.w: Provides enhanced legal certainty and structured liquidity channels for off-plan real estate buyers, reinforcing governance within the property market.

stories.t: SDAIA Signs Nine MoUs, Showcases 12 National Data, AI Projects at LEAP 2026
stories.b: The Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority signed nine memorandums of understanding and presented 12 national data and artificial intelligence initiatives at LEAP 2026.
stories.w: Accelerates the execution of national AI strategies through targeted public-private sector partnerships and localized capability showcases.

stories.t: Stc Bahrain expands enterprise cybersecurity portfolio through strategic Cloudflare partnership
stories.b: stc Bahrain entered into a strategic partnership with Cloudflare to expand its advanced enterprise cybersecurity service offerings.
stories.w: Strengthens enterprise-grade defenses against distributed attacks and data breaches for corporate clients across the Bahraini market.

stories.t: TRA Issues Number Portability Regulatory Framework
stories.b: Oman's Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (TRA) officially issued its comprehensive regulatory framework governing number portability.
stories.w: Enhances consumer protection and fosters fair competitive dynamics among telecom operators within the Sultanate.

themes.t: Massive Enterprise AI and Hyperscale Infrastructure Commitments
themes.b: With technology deal flow at LEAP 2026 approaching $15 billion—anchored by massive investments from major providers like AWS and Microsoft alongside SDAIA's national project showcases—the Gulf is rapidly transitioning from AI experimentation to large-scale operational execution.

themes.t: Liquidity Expansion and Structural Banking Evolution
themes.b: Regional financial markets show healthy expansion, marked by a 7% surge in Saudi banking loans to $944 billion, KIB's $500 million sukuk issuance, and corporate restructurings such as UGB's transition into Burgan Bank Bahrain.

themes.t: Regulatory Harmonization and Modernized Payment Infrastructures
themes.b: GCC central banks are tightening cybersecurity coordination and fintech cooperation, complemented by structural advancements like the Qatar Central Bank enabling direct RTGS access for payment service providers.

ceo.lead: If I were advising the CEO of a Gulf bank or government technology organisation, the three issues I would put on the leadership agenda this week are...
items: Capitalizing on the multi-billion-dollar AI and cloud infrastructure wave to accelerate enterprise productivity without compromising compliance.
Preparing payment and treasury systems for direct RTGS integration and evolving GCC-wide fintech regulatory standards.
Strengthening cross-border cybersecurity governance in lockstep with heightened central bank cooperation frameworks.
